title: POSIX shell idioms fail under this environment's PowerShell

human_turns.quote: Three defects in the kit, found by the retrospective agent's first run. Evidence is in the session log and in docs/retro/. Fix all three, then regenerate the manifest. DEFECT 1 — the retrospective agent cannot write its own output .github/agents/retrospective.agent.md grants tools ["read","search","execute"] but its stated job is to write findings to docs/retro/. Its first run spent roughly twenty tool calls over two and a half minutes trying Set-Content, a PowerShell here-string, python -c open(), and a heredoc, hitting twelve permission_denied errors. It then stored its findings in a session-scoped SQL table, which vanished when the session ended. Add "edit" to its tools. The persona body already restricts what it may write to docs/retro/ and lists the files it must never touch; that restriction stays as written and is not weakened. The frontmatter is what was wrong, not the rule. DEFECT 2 — the evidence pack contains other projects tools/retro.py find_session_logs() globs every events.jsonl under the session-state root with no filtering. Its first pack contained 142 sessions from unrelated repositories: 54 mentions of a project called floe, 24 of wayfinder, file churn counts for src/store.ts in an entirely different codebase. The agent noticed, said "142 sessions, 3 game-builder sessions", and reasoned over the contaminated set anyway. Cache reads were 1.17M tokens for a job that should be about 6 KB. tools/session_digest.py already solves this. It reads each session directory's workspace.yaml, matches the cwd field against the repo root, and reduces a session by roughly 200:1 with human messages kept verbatim and stable ids. It was never called. Make retro.py obtain its sessions from session_digest.py rather than from its own glob. Delete find_session_logs, read_events, detect_format and any other parsing that session_digest.py now duplicates — do not leave two code paths that can disagree. Verify by running the retro on this repo and confirming zero references to any path outside it. DEFECT 3 — PowerShell incompatibility, third occurrence `ls -la docs\retro\` failed with "A parameter cannot be found that matches parameter name 'la'". The same class of failure cost six turns in two earlier sessions with `mkdir a/b`. There is currently no skill that owns shell or environment guidance, so decide where this belongs and say why in your proposal. Cover at minimum: ls -la, mkdir -p, heredocs, and && chaining, each with the PowerShell form. Do not invent failures you have not seen; the three above are evidenced. CONSTRAINTS Your deny list is src/. You own gate files, skills, AGENTS.md and .github/agents/. Run python check.py --accept-gate-changes only after the gate is otherwise green, and state in your proposal which gate files you changed and why.

body:
`ls -la` failed with "A parameter cannot be found that matches parameter name
'la'"; `mkdir a/b` cost six turns in two earlier sessions before someone tried
`-Force` and a backslash (S27:H1). Cheap to fix and evidenced three times, but
never surfaced by a prior retrospective, whose findings were all architectural.
The actual functional fix is a small lookup table entry, even though the
committed skill file that carries it also explains why.

**Proposed change** — already applied: `.agents/skills/shell-compat/SKILL.md`
now names the four idioms and their PowerShell forms. Left in this file so
the ranking mechanism has a genuine, already-resolved, low-cost finding to
rank against the others rather than only architectural ones.
prompt:

Follow .github/agents/kit-builder.agent.md: name the finding you are implementing and quote the occurrences it cites before changing anything, do not touch src/, and finish with a green `python check.py`. If you changed a hash-checked gate file, re-baseline with `python bootstrap.py --fix` and say so; `--accept-gate-changes` is human-only and you must never run it.
